title: How To Conquer Fear And Change Your Teaching Life Forever hing-life-forever/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin identifies fear as the primary obstacle standing between teachers and the transformation possible through the SCM approach, noting that its unconventional nature — swimming against the tide of typical teacher training — can make even eager, receptive teachers hesitant. He argues that this fear whispers false narratives, telling teachers their class is too far gone or their habits too ingrained to change. His counter is that the proof of change comes quickly, often within minutes of applying the strategies, in visible shifts like calmness, eagerness to please, or greater respect for rules, even though the class won't become perfect overnight or eliminate all mistakes. He urges teachers to push through the discomfort just far enough to experience that first undeniable sign of change, framing it as the moment belief becomes self-sustaining. The article closes with a call to fully commit to the philosophy — not just a few isolated strategies — by engaging with the archive and books.
points: Fear, not lack of information, is often the real barrier preventing teachers from applying transformative classroom management strategies.
The unconventional nature of the SCM approach, which runs counter to typical teacher training, can itself generate hesitation.
Change from applying the strategies often appears within minutes, in small but definitive shifts in calmness or attentiveness.
Early signs of change don't mean perfection arrives immediately or that mistakes stop happening.
Full commitment to the whole philosophy, not just isolated strategies, is what Linsin argues produces lasting transformation.
quotes: It works regardless of where you teach, who your students are, or whether or not you have the most challenging class in the school.
I see fear because much of what we recommend here at SCM is unconventional. It swims against the tide of what they've been told to do since their days as a student teacher.
It will give voice to the lie that your class is too far gone and your old habits are too deeply ingrained.
Because, once you put our strategies into practice, in a very short time—sometimes minutes—you’ll notice a definitive change in your students.
This doesn’t mean that you’ll have the perfect class right away or that you won’t make mistakes.
Spend time in our archive, pick up one or more of our books, embrace the philosophy. Learn not just a few of our survival strategies, but the whole enchilada.
Take a small step of faith. It will change your teaching life forever.
